name: PaperOrchestra
cost: Not stated in the README. You pay for the AI model and API calls you use.
short: A Google Research pipeline of AI agents that turns your ideas and experiment logs into a LaTeX research paper draft.
what: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework from Google Cloud AI Research for writing AI research papers. Separate agents handle the outline, literature review, section writing, refinement and plots. It takes your ideas and experiment logs and produces a LaTeX manuscript in a conference template.
who: Researchers who are comfortable with Python and Conda and want to test automated paper drafting. The README says it is not an officially supported Google product, so treat it as research code.
needs: An API key for the model you use: Gemini (or a Vertex AI project) or OpenAI
A Semantic Scholar API key, for the literature search
A folder with your raw materials and a LaTeX template folder

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.text: Run this in the cloned repo.

steps.title: Add your keys
steps.text: Create a `.env` file in the project root with the keys for the models you use, such as `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY`.

steps.title: Run the pipeline
steps.text: Point it at your raw materials, a LaTeX template such as `templates/cvpr2025` and an output folder. Add `--use_plotting true` to have it make figures.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `python paper_writing_cli.py` with `--raw_materials_dir`, `--latex_template_dir`, `--output_dir` and `--use_plotting true` set to your own folders.

watch: Your keys live in a plain `.env` file. Keep it out of version control.
The optional demo can email results to you, which needs your email address and password in `.env`. Skip it if you would rather not store those.
The dataset used in the paper is not in the repo yet. The README says it will be released later.
Every run calls paid model APIs, so watch your usage.
